output.brief: The slowdown is not mainly about Corvane or the new hires. Stage timings show it sits in one place: collateral valuation for property-secured loans. That stage went from about 1.7 days in April to 7.6 in June and 8.4 in August. Unsecured loans are back to about 6 days. Consumer loans on the same system are flat. Document collection, underwriting and decision times are flat, including at the branches with new hires. The valuation jump follows Credit Policy v14 on 1 May. That policy cut the threshold for a mandatory full appraisal from $500k to $150k, and nobody assessed its effect on processing time. The valuation firm's contract renewal on 1 April did not move the stage in April, so it is a weaker suspect. I did not check the firm's own service data, so it can't be fully ruled out. Many withdrawals are auto-closures from a new 30-day rule, so the withdrawal rise is partly a counting change. Next steps: take the measured delay and the audit rationale to the credit risk committee to decide on the appraisal threshold. Add a by-stage view to the dashboard. Don't withhold the Corvane payment or put the new hires on improvement plans. Hold any customer-incentive offer until the withdrawal picture is clearer.
